where: i1-core-math: tests/unit/i1-core-math.test.mjs (U20, U26) versus design 5.7 and 5.8
problem: [minor] Several mutants survive in my mutation run, so a few design rules have no pinned test. (a) `neg` without `wrap(arg, 3)` in toTex survives; the output would then print `-(z+1)` as `-z + 1`, which is wrong maths that KaTeX still renders. No row covers a negated sum or product. (b) FRAC_QMAX 24 to 60 and SURD_QMAX 4 to 12 survive. (c) asSurd tolerance loosened from 1e-10 to 1e-3 survives, so a decimal like 1.4143 could be mislabelled as sqrt(2). The code itself is correct: I checked texNumber(1/25) = 0.04, texNumber(1/24) = \frac{1}{24}, texNumber(S2/5) = 0.283, texNumber(1.4142) = 1.414, and toTex('-(z+1)') = -\left(z + 1\right).

where: i1-core-math: js/core/complex.js div(), inv() (and pow with n < 0), wrapArg()
problem: [minor] Robustness at astronomical magnitudes, outside anything a student can reach. div and inv use b.re^2 + b.im^2 as the zero test, so any divisor with |b| below about 1.5e-162 is treated as zero and returns NaN (inv(1e-200) and div(1, 1e-200) both give {NaN, NaN}). Any divisor with |b| above about 1.3e154 overflows, so div(1e200, 1e200) gives {NaN, 0} instead of 1. wrapArg(1.7e308) returns -2e292, outside (-pi, pi]. These bend contract 2.2(3), NaN only for undefined input, and the wrapArg range promise.
fix: Optional. Scale by max(|b.re|, |b.im|) before squaring, and test for zero on the parts, not on the square. Or add one sentence to design 2.2 saying results are exact only for 1e-150 < |z| < 1e150.

where: i1-core-math: tests/unit/i1-core-math.test.mjs (U26 toTex rows, U-tests for compile)
problem: [minor] Three of my 30 mutants survive the 31 tests. (1) toTex negation bracketing: the mutant that stops wrapping -(z+1) prints `-z + 1`, a wrong formula, and no test fails. (2) The product right-operand wrap threshold: the mutant prints `2-z` for `2*-z`, again a wrong formula, with no failure. (3) A constant integer exponent such as z^2 switched from pow to powc: z^2 at i would give im 1.2e-16 instead of exactly 0, with no failure. The shipped code is correct in all three cases: toTex gives `-\left(z + 1\right)`, `2\left(-z\right)` and `z \cdot \left(-z\right)`, and evaluate('z^2', i) gives exactly {-1, 0}. The gap is test strength only.
fix: Add pinned rows: toTex('-(z+1)') => '-\left(z + 1\right)', toTex('-(z*z)'), toTex('2*-z') => '2\left(-z\right)', toTex('z*-z'), toTex('z/-z'). Add a strict-equality row: evaluate('z^2', {re:0,im:1}) deep-equals {re:-1,im:0}, and the same for z^3 at i.

where: i1-data: tests/unit/i1-data.test.mjs 'A4: every decimal in the copy is a checked value'
problem: [minor] The regex `(?<![\d.])\d+\.\d+(?![\d.])` skips any decimal followed by a sentence-ending period, so the allow-list guard has a gap. Two prose decimals escape it: '≈ 5.385.' in 1.2.2 cart and '≈ 0.309.' in 1.4.1 cart. Both values are correct, but a mutation changing 0.309. to 0.390. passes all 30 tests. Numbers inside routes sentences are otherwise unpinned: 4 of 5 prose mutants survived (5π/3 changed to 4π/3, 'ρ(1 + cos φ) = 8' changed to 9, a wrong CR sign, a wrong discriminant). The design acknowledged this for wording in its risk list (9.1), not for numbers. The current prose is all correct, which I verified by hand.
fix: Change the lookahead to `(?!\d)` plus a check that a trailing '.' is not followed by a digit, so sentence-final decimals are caught. Optionally add a small pin of the key integers and fractions in routes.

problem: [minor] `addressLabel('C', null)` throws TypeError ('Cannot read properties of null (reading short)') because `{ short = false } = {}` does not default null. The first-argument edge cases are all fine: undefined, 42, {}, 'constructor', 'toString'. The design's 'never throws on wrong argument type' is therefore not absolute.
fix: Accept `opts` as a plain parameter, e.g. `addressLabel(code, opts) { const short = !!(opts && opts.short); ... }`, and add the null case to the A1 address-helpers test.

problem: [minor] Extreme inputs freeze the page. `sector({theta0: 1e17, theta1: 1e17})` and `sector({theta0: 2e16, theta1: 0})` never return, because th1 + 2pi == th1 in floating point. `sector({theta0: 1e10, theta1: 0})` takes 1.2 s. `n`, `nPerSide`, `rings`, `rays` and the fill counts have no upper bound: `segment(0,1,{n:3e6})` takes 1 s and `polarGrid({rings:2e5, rays:0})` takes 9 s. Design 8.1 says these edge cases are handled and `none throw`. The Lab probably bounds its sliders, but a typed value would hang the tab.

where: i1-core-mapping: js/core/mapping.js run(), pole-leap rule (a) (design 5.2 step 7, X2a)
problem: [minor] A hand-jittered freehand stroke can be cut where nothing goes to infinity. A candidate step has stretch > 3 times the median and the path reverses (turn > 90 degrees) at both ends. With pixel-level jitter that happens whenever |f'| is more than 3 times its median along the stroke. Random walks with jitter of 0.005 (about half a pixel at 100 px/unit) and a 0.01 minDist gave extra pieces in 26 of 300 strokes under z^3, 34 of 300 under e^z, 28 of 300 under the Joukowski map and 7 of 300 under sin z. At 0.01 jitter it was 51, 74, 103 and 28 of 300. In a 400-stroke e^z sample the gaps were at most 2.7% of the image extent and at most 1.5% of t, and 7 strokes lost an end. The w-plane cursor (`pointOnPieces`) flickers null inside such a gap. The new teleport rule (b) is not the cause: results are identical with it disabled. It is a design-level limitation of the reversal rule that the earlier review already accepted, and the damage is small.
fix: Optional. Require a near-total reversal (turn > about 150 degrees) at both ends, or also require |dw| to exceed some fraction of the image extent. Or tell the Lab to smooth or resample freehand strokes (`resample`) before `pushForward`. At minimum record the limitation in design 8.1.

where: i1-core-three: createView3D loop: renderNow and contextLost (5.12)
problem: [minor] While the context is lost, `renderNow()` returns early without clearing `needsRender`. The loop therefore reschedules every animation frame until the context is restored and never goes dormant. It is harmless but wasteful.
fix: In `renderNow`, clear `needsRender` when `contextLost` is true, or have `loop` skip scheduling while `contextLost` is true. `onContextRestored` already calls `requestRender()`.

problem: [minor] The visible text is `Reset view` but the accessible name is `Reset the 3D view to its starting angle`. The name does not contain the visible label, which is WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name. A voice-control user saying `click Reset view` would not match. The design mandated this string, so it is a design nit, not a build error.
fix: Use `aria-label="Reset view: back to the starting angle"`, or drop the `aria-label` and rely on the visible text.

problem: [minor] Any wheel event over the container hides the hint, even when the wheel only scrolls the page past the view, and any keydown does too, including Tab. A student scrolling past the picture loses the 'Click the view, then scroll to zoom' hint before reading it. This matches the design text, but it is poor behaviour.
fix: Hide the hint on wheel only when the event is actually handled (container focused, or Ctrl/Cmd held). Hide on keydown only for handled keys.

problem: [minor] The hint inset is measured once, in `fitTo`. If the container is later resized (phone rotation, a narrower layout) and the hint re-wraps from two lines to one or the reverse, the shift of the picture stays stale until the next `fitTo()`. The picture is then slightly off-centre.
fix: Optional: in `resize()`, when the hint is still visible, recompute the inset and update `viewShift`. Otherwise note it for stations.

problem: [minor] The time dots are default `THREE.Points` (`PointsMaterial` size 6), which render as small squares in every screenshot. The round-dot language used elsewhere (beads, floor point, markers) is lost on the sphere.
fix: Use a round alpha-masked point sprite texture, or small spheres, for the five time dots. It is cosmetic.
